long_biography.plain_text:
Bruno Michel entered top-level motorsport with Ligier, working within the French Formula 1 team before moving into driver development and management. He guided talents including Fernando Alonso and Mark Webber. That experience gave him a close view of the preparation required to move promising racers toward the sport's highest level.

With Flavio Briatore, Michel created GP2 as the successor to Formula 3000 and developed it into the principal feeder category beneath Formula 1. He now serves as chief executive of FIA Formula 2 and Formula 3, while also handling F1 Academy operations. His remit includes championship formats, technical direction, cost control and progression through the single-seater ladder.
